narrative:
The model determined that you have a 47% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough to cross the bank's approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the purpose of the loan, the amount you requested, and the status of your checking account. The fact that you are financing a new car pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk, as new-car loans are associated with higher risk in the bank's experience. Your requested loan of 6,260 DM was more than twice the average amount approved applicants ask for; this larger sum also increased the model's estimate of risk. Finally, having a checking-account balance between 0 and 200 DM worked against you. While many approved applicants have no checking account at all, those who do maintain only small balances like yours tend to be viewed as higher risk.

Taken together, these three factors outweighed several positive signals such as your solid credit history of existing paid loans and your stable employment of 4–7 years.

To improve your chances on a future application, consider requesting a smaller loan amount, saving until you can show a stronger checking-account balance, or exploring a different purpose that the bank sees as lower risk. Reviewing your full credit report and speaking with a loan officer about ways to strengthen your profile would be a good next step. (218 words)
